newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ASTROS' PITCHER SID FERNANDEZ ANNOUNCES RETIREMENT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ASTROS' PITCHER SID FERNANDEZ ANNOUNCES RETIREMENT.

text.p: Houston Astros left-hander Sid Fernandez, a two-time All-Star and 16-year major league veteran, on Friday abandoned his attempted comeback from an elbow injury and announced his retirement.
The 34-year-old Fernandez signed with the Astros as a free agent this past offseason but was limited to just one appearance due to an arthritic condition in his left elbow that required surgery.
The Astros currently lead the National League Central and the team had hoped that Fernandez would be available for the stretch run.

"Even though he was only able to make one start this season, I believe he still had an impact on our team with his presence and experience in pennant races," said Astros general manager Gerry Hunsicker. "His numbers last season showed he was still a capable major league pitcher when he was healthy."
Fernandez was 3-6 in 11 games for the Philadelphia Phillies in 1996.
Born in Honolulu, Fernandez finished his career with a 114-96 record and a 3.36 ERA in 307 games for Los Angeles, the New York Mets, Baltimore, Philadelphia and Houston.

Fernandez was named to the National League All-Star team in 1986 and 1987 for the Mets. He was outstanding in his lone World Series appearance, allowing one run over 6 2/3 innings in three relief outings for the victorious Mets against the Boston Red Sox in 1986.
